title: Brand Sprint vs Agency
description: Compare a one-week $3,000 senior Brand Sprint with traditional agencies ($25k–$100k+, 3–9 months) and sub-$3k marketplace clutter (~$750–$2.3k). A founder decision framework for when each wins.
body:
Hiring branding help usually lands you in one of two stories.

Story A: a traditional agency — big proposal, long timeline, account managers, and a bill that starts in the tens of thousands.

Story B: a focused Brand Sprint — one senior designer, one week for core identity, a clear price, and you stay in the room for every decision.

This guide is for founders, owners, and marketers who have to pick a path — not for designers debating process theory.

I'm Arek Dvornechuck, a senior brand designer in New York.

At Ebaq Design you work directly with me.

Below is the same comparison I use on calls: when a sprint wins, when an agency still makes sense, and when neither is the right spend.

Key takeaways

  • Traditional agencies commonly sit at $25k–$100k+ and 3–9 months or more.
  • Ebaq's Brand Sprint is $3,000 for one week of focused identity work (ongoing work from $10,000/mo).
  • Sprint wins when you need speed, senior judgment, and a buyer-ready identity without agency layers.
  • Not every "sprint" is the same product: public Contra listings now run from direction sprints about $750 and 72-hour sprints around $900 to one- and two-week brand sprints roughly $1,500–$2,300 — that is market noise; Ebaq competes on senior craft, motion, and interactive web.
  • Agency still fits multi-market rollouts, large stakeholder theaters, and scopes that need a bench.
  • Neither fits when the real constraint is sales, product, or timing — not the look.
  • Settle whether you need a rebrand at all before you hire anyone (refresh vs rebrand).

What each option actually is

Traditional agency

A traditional agency packages strategy, creative, account management, and often a junior bench behind a senior lead.

You get process, decks, and capacity for big rollouts.

You also get handoffs, waiting for feedback loops, and a price that reflects the overhead.

On the Ebaq site comparison, that model lands at $25k–$100k+, 3–9 months or more, with account managers and junior designers in the mix.

Brand Sprint (Ebaq)

A Brand Sprint is a focused identity engagement: strategy into a custom logo and identity system you can actually use — typically in about one week for the core brand.

At Ebaq Design the flagship is $3,000 for one week.

Broader ongoing work typically starts at $10,000 per month.

You work directly with a senior designer — no account manager layer between you and the work.

Website, motion, and rollout extras are scoped separately when you need them.

For a fuller money map, try the branding cost calculator.

That is not a dig at every agency.

It is a filter for startups that cannot afford nine months of sameness while the market moves.

Brand sprint vs freelancer vs agency

Most founders are really choosing between three models, not two.

Freelancer and agency ranges come from published packages I checked for my guide to what a complete brand identity costs.

The real difference is not talent but how many people and meetings sit between you and the designer.

Not all sprints are the same sprint

There is a third option founders now see first: the cheap one-week sprint listing.

On Contra alone, October 2026 public listings include direction sprints as low as about $750, 72-hour identity sprints around $900, and one- to two-week brand sprints roughly $1,500–$2,300.

That is market noise — other sellers' prices — not a cheaper version of Ebaq.

At the other end, studio sprints publish much higher numbers: Proof of Work $15,000 / 2 weeks (competitor-stated), PIXELUP $15,000 (competitor-stated), and Primary $50k / 2 weeks (competitor-stated). Splash Creative lists Focused ~$8k, Identity ~$12k, Brand + Web $25k–$75k, and a $7,500 two-week AI Implementation Sprint (competitor-stated). Crafted's public FAQ is live again at $25k–$60k focused / $100k+ full brand-and-build (competitor-stated, October 2026).

The $3,000 Brand Sprint sits in the middle on purpose — above commodity clutter, below agency and premium-sprint stickers.

What separates it from the sub-$3k listings:

  • Senior, direct — one senior designer in New York, no junior handoff.
  • Designed to move — I do brand motion, so the identity is built for animation, product UI, and launch content.
  • Designed for interactive web — I build Framer, Webflow, and React sites, so the system is made for a real site from day one.
  • Anti-sameness — the goal is a brand buyers remember, not a template that looks like every peer.

Decision rule: if price is the only filter, a listing will win; if the brand has to carry sales and fundraising, compare seniority and what ships.

When a Brand Sprint wins

Choose a sprint when speed and senior judgment are the product.

You are pre-seed to Series B (or a boutique firm) and need an investor-ready or launch-ready identity without waiting a quarter.

You already know roughly who you serve — or you can lock positioning in the first conversations — and you need the look to catch up.

Marketplace or junior freelancers already burned months; you want one accountable senior, not another round of guessing.

Your site or pitch looks like every peer in the category and you need distinctive cues now, not after a long research theater.

Decision rule: if a clear identity system in about a week would unblock sales, hiring, or fundraising, the sprint is usually the sharper tool.

When a traditional agency still makes sense

Agencies earn their keep on scale and coordination, not on every logo.

You have many stakeholders, regions, or product lines that need parallel workstreams and a dedicated account layer.

The scope is packaging, retail, vehicles, events, and global guidelines — not just a startup identity and site.

Procurement or board process requires a multi-person team on paper.

You want a long retainer with specialists (media, PR, performance) under one roof, and branding is only one workstream.

Decision rule: if the hard problem is coordinating a large organization — not getting to a sharp identity fast — an agency can still be the right buy.

If that is you, compare stage fit, prices and timelines in my list of startup branding agencies.

Just compare scopes, not logos on a moodboard.

Ask what is in and out: identity only, messaging, website design, implementation, and rollout.

When neither is right

This is the answer teams under-use.

A new identity will not fix a broken offer, a missing sales motion, or a product that is not ready to show.

If leadership cannot state who you are for in one sentence, spend on positioning clarity first — not on a logo bake-off.

If the brand is fine and the website is the real drag, scope a site project instead of a full agency rebrand.

If you are still deciding whether to rebrand, refresh, or wait, settle that before you book anyone.

Decision rule: if the constraint is not the brand, do not buy branding theater to soothe anxiety.

Cost and timeline — only what is public

Stick to stated numbers so you can compare honestly.

Ebaq Design (Brand Sprint / focused engagement)

  • Focused engagements start at $3,000 for one week.
  • Broader ongoing work typically starts at $10,000 per month.
  • Comparison framing: $3k/wk or $10k/mo, 1 week to brand, direct senior designer.

Traditional agency (stated comparison)

  • $25k–$100k+
  • 3–9 months or more
  • Account managers and junior designers in the delivery chain

Public peer anchors (competitor-stated)

  • Proof of Work Brand Sprint: $15,000 / 2 weeks
  • Primary: $50k / 2 weeks
  • Crafted (NYC agency): $25k–$60k focused, $100k+ full brand-and-build, identity ~4–6 weeks (public FAQ live again October 2026)

Sub-$3k marketplace clutter (~$750 direction kits, ~$900 72-hour sprints, through ~$1.5k–$2.3k one- and two-week sprints) exists too — treat it as a different product, not as a benchmark for senior work.

Website builds (Framer, Webflow, or React) and motion are separate scopes when you need them — same as most serious studios.

For how those pieces stack in a buyer budget, see the branding cost calculator above.

Decision framework (one page)

Ask these in order.

1. Is the constraint actually the brand?

If no → neither. Fix sales, product, or timing first.

2. Do you need a large bench and multi-quarter coordination?

If yes → agency (or a scoped retainer that explicitly includes that bench).

3. Do you need a distinctive, usable identity system in about a week, with senior access?

If yes → Brand Sprint.

4. Are you still unsure rebrand vs refresh vs wait?

Pause hiring. Book a short call to pressure-test scope.

5. Does your category already look identical?

If yes — especially AI/SaaS — treat distinctiveness as a go-to-market risk, not a cosmetic upgrade.

FAQ

Is a Brand Sprint "cheap branding"?

No.

Cheap is marketplace roulette and junior guesswork.

A sprint is focused senior work at a clear price — not an agency overhead stack.

Why not a $750–$2,300 marketplace sprint?

If you only need a quick direction kit or a basic mark, a cheaper listing may be enough.

If you need a system that holds up in motion, on an interactive site, and in front of buyers, ask who designs it and what happens when you need the next piece.

The $3,000 Brand Sprint is senior-direct, with motion and web in the same studio.

Can a sprint replace a full agency AOR?

Not if you need media buying, PR, and a ten-person team.

Yes if your near-term need is identity (and optionally a site) done with judgment and speed.

What if we need a website too?

Identity first when the look is broken.

Then scope the site — Framer, Webflow, or React — as a follow-on, not as a surprise add-on mid-sprint.

What if we only have a few weeks before a raise or launch?

That is exactly when agency timelines of 3–9 months fail founders.

A one-week core identity is built for that window — if you can decide quickly.

How do we start?

Book a short intro call.

We confirm fit, timing, and whether a sprint, ongoing work, or neither is the honest answer.

Pick the model that matches the job

Agencies are built for scale and theater.

A Brand Sprint is built for speed and senior craft.

Neither is built to fix a business problem that is not the brand.
